result.question:
CONTEXT: The Razorpay AI Buildathon 2026 (razorpay.com/buildathon/) is a student-only hiring funnel for a 6/12-month "AI Builder Internship" (Rs 75,000/month, in-person Bangalore, from September 2026). Applicants pick ONE of 5 tracks (Track 1: AI Growth & Agentic Commerce; Track 2: AI Risk Manager; Track 3: AI Revenue Recovery; Track 4: AI Finance Controller; Open Track), build a project, and submit via a Google Form (title "Razorpay AI Builder Internship 2026") with: Selected Track, Project Name, Project Objectives, public GitHub Repository URL, 5-min Pitch Video Link, and "Build Challenges & Technical Obstacles". Shortlisted builders go to a panel interview. Today is 2026-08-24.

GOAL: Validate/falsify the following specific claims, and surface anything a competitor would know that is missing.

CLAIMS TO VERIFY OR REFUTE (each is a falsifiable factual claim):
1. The application deadline is 5 September 2026. (This is NOT published on razorpay.com/buildathon/ nor in the application form — only in third-party aggregator blogs. Find any authoritative confirmation or contradiction, including Razorpay's official LinkedIn/X/Instagram posts, or any extended/changed deadline.)
2. Submission is individual, not team-based (the official form has no team fields). Find any Razorpay statement about team size or collaboration.
3. There is no published judging rubric or scoring weights beyond the five per-track "The bar" statements on the official page.
4. Razorpay Agent Studio (razorpay.com/agent-studio) is in beta/early access and ships exactly these 7 prebuilt agents: Dispute Responder, Subscription Recovery, Abandoned Cart Conversion, RTO Shield, RTO Insights, Settlement Insights, Cashflow Forecaster — and is built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.
5. Razorpay has live agentic payment pilots: agentic UPI on Claude with Zepto/Swiggy/Zomato (with NPCI), in-app checkout with Vodafone, voice-AI payments with Gnani.ai and SuperU, and international payments with Replit.
6. Razorpay's payments foundation model is called "Vulcan", trained on ~4 billion customer-to-merchant payments per year, targeting routing, fraud detection and checkout conversion.
7. Razorpay's official MCP server (github.com/razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server) exposes roughly 45 tools and supports test-mode API keys (rzp_test_...).
8. NPCI's Unified Agent Protocol (UAP) for agentic UPI payments has NOT yet launched and requires RBI approval.

GAPS TO FILL (research these — this is the higher-value half):
A. What can a developer ACTUALLY simulate in Razorpay TEST MODE? Specifically: can you simulate failed payments and specific failure/error codes, UPI mandate/AutoPay failures, chargebacks/disputes, settlements and settlement reconciliation reports, refunds, and webhooks? Find Razorpay's official docs on test mode, test cards, simulated failures, error code lists, and webhook simulation. This determines what is buildable in ~12 days.
B. Razorpay's official error/failure code taxonomy and any published payment-failure reason codes, UPI decline codes, or NPCI UPI error codes that a "payment degradation root cause" agent could reason over.
C. Public, legally usable datasets a student could use for: chargeback/dispute prediction, payment fraud, RTO/COD return prediction in India, invoice/receivables collection, and bank-statement-to-invoice reconciliation. Note licences.
D. COMPETITOR RECON: search GitHub, Devpost, LinkedIn, X/Twitter and YouTube for any projects, repos or pitch videos already published for the Razorpay AI Buildathon 2026 (search terms like "razorpay buildathon", "razorpay ai builder internship", "razorpay agentic commerce project"). What are people building, and how good is it?
E. What do Razorpay engineers/leaders (e.g. Harshil Mathur, Shashank Kumar, or Razorpay engineering/AI leads) say publicly in 2026 about what they look for in AI builders, what makes a project have "signal", and what Razorpay's current AI priorities are? Find Razorpay engineering blog posts and podcast/interview statements from 2026.
F. Razorpay's publicly stated business problems and metrics in 2025-2026: payment success rates, UPI failure rates, RTO/COD return rates in Indian e-commerce, chargeback volumes, DSO/receivables problems for Indian SMEs, reconciliation effort. Prefer numbers from Razorpay reports (e.g. "The Era of Rising Bharat"/state-of-payments style reports), NPCI data, or RBI data.
G. Best practices in 2026 for EVALUATING an AI agent that takes actions: agent eval harnesses, trace/observability standards, tool-call evaluation, and what "audit trail" means in a regulated payments context. Include any RBI/regulatory constraints on autonomous agents moving money in India (e.g. AA framework, e-mandate rules, delegated payments, UPI Circle).
H. Any past Razorpay hackathon/internship winners or AI Builder interns — what did they build, and is there any public account of why they were selected?

OUTPUT: a cited report that (1) marks each numbered claim CONFIRMED / REFUTED / UNVERIFIED with evidence, and (2) gives concrete, specific, actionable findings for each lettered gap, with URLs.
result.summary: Of the eight numbered claims, four are CONFIRMED outright (no published rubric; Agent Studio built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK and gated behind early access; Razorpay Vulcan as the named payments foundation model; the MCP server's test-mode key handling), two are CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTIONS (the 7-agent roster is really 8 tiles / 7 distinct agents, and the MCP tool count is exactly 45 in the repo versus "35+" in Razorpay's docs), one is PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (agentic UPI on Claude with NPCI and Zomato/Swiggy/Zepto is real but is a closed pilot on UPI Reserve Pay, while the Vodafone, Gnani.ai, SuperU and Replit pilots were not independently verified in this pass), and two remain UNVERIFIED against any Razorpay source (the 5 September 2026 deadline, which appears only in aggregator blogs and one non-Razorpay X post, and the individual-vs-team rule, which is nowhere stated). The single most decision-relevant negative finding is that razorpay.com/buildathon/ publishes no deadline, no rubric, no scoring weights and no team-size policy at all — evaluation is expressed only as one qualitative "the bar" sentence per track plus an undefined "signal" gate, so competitors are working from the same information vacuum and third-party blogs inventing four-parameter rubrics ("Problem Taste, Build Quality, AI Judgment, Failure Recovery") are fabricating. A second correction matters for build planning: the widely repeated idea that the official page scopes builds to "Razorpay test-mode APIs" was REFUTED — that constraint is not on the page, so test-mode limits are a practical constraint rather than a stated rule. Of the eight lettered gaps, only Gap B (error/failure-code taxonomy) was substantively filled and it was filled well: Razorpay publishes a structured, machine-readable, method-specific error taxonomy with a `source` attribution field and a downloadable reason spreadsheet, which is the strongest ready-made substrate found for a "payment degradation root cause" agent.

findings.claim: Claim 1 (5 September 2026 deadline) — UNVERIFIED. The official Razorpay Buildathon page publishes NO application deadline; the only temporal references are to the internship START ("In-person, Bangalore, from September"). The Google Form is likewise deadline-free. Every source asserting 5 September is a non-Razorpay aggregator blog or an individual X user.
findings.evidence: Raw curl of the buildathon page (55,250 bytes) with script/style stripped yields exactly two temporal references, both about internship start: hero "Students only. 6 or 12 month AI Builder Internship. In-person, Bangalore, from September." and the offer block "Rs 75,000 (monthly stipend) - 6 or 12 (months, your choice) - In-person (Bangalore, from September)." Case-insensitive grep for september|deadline|close|last date|apply by|submit by|timeline|august|2026 returned no date string, no countdown, no "applications close". The only CTA is "Apply now" -> forms.gle/d9r2gvxp8cmoZhon9, which 302s to a Google Form titled "Razorpay AI Builder Internship 2026" with no description and fields Email / Full Name / College Name / Graduation Year / "In-person Internship availability starting September" — again a start-date, no deadline. Three separate searches for an authoritative deadline surfaced only velonx.in, offcampusjobs4u.com, coursejoiner.com, jobseekershub.co.in, placement-officer.com, fresherjobinfo.in, thejobcompany.co.in and one X user. SCOPE CAVEAT: Razorpay's LinkedIn/Instagram feeds could not be read directly, so a social post stating 5 September cannot be excluded. PRACTICAL IMPLICATION: treat 5 Sept 2026 as an unverified soft deadline and submit early — an unpublished deadline is equally consistent with rolling review.

findings.claim: Claim 3 (no published judging rubric) — CONFIRMED. There is no rubric, no scoring weights, no percentages and no numerical criteria anywhere on the official page. Evaluation is expressed as exactly one qualitative "the bar" sentence per track, plus an undefined "signal" gate. Third-party blogs claiming a four-parameter rubric are fabricating.
findings.evidence: Three targeted fetches of the official page; keyword audit returned NO for rubric, score, weight, %, points, criteria — and no "Problem Taste", "Build Quality", "AI Judgment", "Failure Recovery". Page structure is: header/intro, five tracks (title, description, "Why now", example directions, "the bar"), the offer, Apply link. The five bars verbatim: Track 01 "Every money action explainable, bounded and gated. Show the audit trail and one failure handled gracefully."; Track 02 "Honest metrics including false-positive cost. Strictly defense-only: anything offense-capable is disqualified."; Track 03 "Don't just identify the problem. Show measured money recovered across a batch, with compliant escalation, stopping rules, and an audit trail."; Track 04 "Throughput plus measured accuracy plus an honest exception list. One cherry-picked match proves nothing."; Track 05 (Open) "Show a real problem, a working product, meaningful use of AI, and evidence that it creates value." Apparent counter-evidence (fresherjobinfo.in, coursejoiner.com asserting "four key parameters: Problem Taste, Build Quality, AI Judgment, Failure Recovery") is not a refutation: none of those strings exist on the official page, fresherjobinfo.in returns HTTP 403 and cites no source, and velonx.in explicitly frames its "architecture, code quality, ability to explain your build" line as its own interpretation. QUALIFICATION: two evaluation-adjacent signals do exist beyond the bars — the process line "pick a track, build something real, show your work (a public repo, a 5 minute pitch video, the architecture), and if it has signal we call you in", plus "No resume screening... No aptitude test. No group discussion" and the form's "Build Challenges & Technical Obstacles" field. None is a rubric. ACTIONABLE: the five bars ARE the rubric — every one demands measured outcomes over a batch, honest failure accounting, and (for Tracks 01 and 03) an explicit audit trail.

findings.claim: Claim 2 (individual vs team submission) — UNVERIFIED. Razorpay has made no statement on team size or collaboration. The official page never uses the words team, solo, individual, collaborate or group in any buildathon context; the individual-submission inference rests only on the absence of team fields in the Google Form.
findings.evidence: Case-insensitive grep of the 55,250-byte raw page: "teams" appears once and only inside the site-wide product-catalog JSON ("Field sales teams", Razorpay POS); "Individual" appears once, also in that JSON ("Individual sellers", Payment Buttons); "group" appears twice — once in the Segment analytics method list, once as "No aptitude test. No group discussion." (interview format, not team formation). "solo", "collaborate", "team size", "per team" — zero occurrences. All buildathon copy is second-person singular in tone: "build something real", "show your work", "Your code speaks louder than your resume." Independent corroboration of the same negative: velonx.in states verbatim "Razorpay's public communication about the buildathon doesn't specify team size requirements. Confirm this on the official application page before you start building."; placement-officer.com carries no team language and advises verifying with Razorpay. Searches targeted at LinkedIn/X/Instagram surfaced stipend, tracks and the alleged 5 Sept date but no team-size statement. CAVEAT: English "you" is number-ambiguous, so singular framing is a tonal reading not a grammatical proof; and the "no team fields in the form" half came from supplied context and was not independently re-fetched in this pass.

findings.claim: Claim 4, SDK half — CONFIRMED from two independent primary Razorpay properties: Agent Studio is built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, announced at FTX'26 in Bengaluru on 12 March 2026.
findings.evidence: Blog verbatim: "Built on **Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK,** the Agentic Studio introduces a reality where a business can deploy a workforce of autonomous agents designed to observe, reason, and execute complex financial operations on your behalf." Newsroom verbatim: Razorpay "introduced the Razorpay Agent Studio – a B2B agent marketplace and builder platform for Payments and Business Banking, built using the Claude Agent SDK from Anthropic", and separately that the Agentic Experience Platform is "an AI-native layer built with Claude." Two adversarial searches probing for a model-provider switch (OpenAI/Gemini/multi-model) returned zero evidence of any change through Aug 2026. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS: every third-party outlet is demonstrably reprinting the same FTX'26 release rather than independently verifying the stack, and razorpay.com/agent-studio itself omits the attribution (that page is JS-rendered and fetched as nav chrome only, so its silence is a fetch artifact, not counter-evidence). Correct epistemic status: "Razorpay states it is built on the Claude Agent SDK" — which is exactly what the claim asserts. STRATEGIC IMPLICATION FOR A SUBMISSION: building on the Claude Agent SDK is stack-aligned with the judges' own product.

findings.claim: Claim 4, agent-roster half — CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTION. The launch blog enumerates EIGHT tiles but only SEVEN distinct agents, exactly matching the claimed list, because Abandoned Cart Conversion appears twice — once "Powered by SuperU" and once "Powered by Nugget by Zomato". The FTX'26 newsroom release names only FOUR of them, so the 7-agent figure is supported by the blog and product page, not by the press release.
findings.vote: 3-0 confirmed; a competing 'only four agents' claim was voted down 0-3
findings.evidence: Two independently worded fetches of the blog returned the identical "Launching Pre-Built Agents for your Business" list of 8 entries: (1) Dispute Responder — "Auto-responds to chargebacks with optimized evidence to maximize dispute win rates." (2) Subscription Recovery — "Analyzes failed subscription payments, apply smarter retry logic, and trigger targeted customer nudges." (3) Abandoned Cart Conversion (Powered by SuperU) (4) Abandoned Cart Conversion (Powered by Nugget by Zomato) — verbatim identical description to (3) (5) Cashflow Forecaster — "Predicts cash position 3-7 days ahead with alerts for payroll risk, shortfalls, and payout failures." (6) RTO Shield — "Detects high-risk COD orders before dispatch using LLM address validation and bad pincode intelligence." (7) RTO Insights — "Analyzes RTO patterns across pincodes, products, and customers to identify preventable return drivers." (8) Settlement Insights — "Sends a daily settlement summary via WhatsApp to track payouts without checking dashboards." Independent corroboration: buildfastwithai.com states "Razorpay debuted eight production-ready agents at FTX 2026" and on the cart agent "Razorpay is launching two variants of this agent, both targeting the same problem". CAVEATS: the newsroom release names only Abandoned Cart Conversion, Dispute Responder, Subscription Recovery and Cashflow Forecaster — the source discrepancy is real and a competitor citing only the press release would report four; the live razorpay.com/agent-studio roster could not be re-verified today because the page is JS-rendered, so the confirmed snapshot is the 12 March 2026 launch set; and de-duplicating the SuperU and Nugget variants into one agent is an interpretive choice. STRATEGIC IMPLICATION: these seven agents are the solution space Razorpay has already built — a submission that merely re-implements Dispute Responder, RTO Shield or Cashflow Forecaster is competing with the judges' own shipped product.

findings.claim: Claim 4, beta/early-access half — CONFIRMED. Agent Studio is not generally available: the live product page still shows "Get early access" as of 2026-08-24, and the custom-agent builder is explicitly badged Beta. Note the FTX'26 press release calls the agents "production-ready", a tonal conflict with the product page.
findings.vote: 3-0 confirmed; a competing 'no beta statement exists' claim was voted down 0-3
findings.evidence: Live product page fetched 2026-08-24 (title "Razorpay Agent Studio | AI Agents for Payments & Revenue Operations"): primary CTA "Get early access" in a top banner, "Sign Up Now" on each agent card, plus "Build With Us"; the "Build your agent from scratch" option is badged "Beta". Blog fetched same day: repeated "Sign Up for Early Access" / "Get Early Access" CTAs and the phrase "No-Code Agent Builder (beta)". Searches for GA/rollout announcements returned only launch-era coverage of 12 Mar 2026 and no exit-from-early-access. Reliability note: a vendor under-claiming availability is a statement against marketing interest, so the direction of the bias supports rather than undermines the finding. CAVEATS: "early access" is a commercial status, not a technical gate — partner-branded variants (SuperU, Nugget by Zomato) may be in genuine production for some merchants; and the newsroom release's "production-ready" language conflicts in tone, which is why the strict reading is "early access commercially, production-grade technically". Status is time-sensitive — re-check before citing it in a submission.

findings.claim: Claim 5, agentic-UPI-on-Claude half — CONFIRMED, with the important correction that it is a closed pilot running on NPCI's UPI Reserve Pay (one-time per-merchant consent, no per-transaction PIN), NOT on the unlaunched Unified Agent Protocol. Merchants are exactly Zomato, Swiggy and Zepto. Announced at the India AI Impact Summit, New Delhi, 20 February 2026.
findings.evidence: Primary blog verbatim: "At the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on February 20, 2026, Razorpay and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) officially announced a partnership to bring Agentic Payments to Claude."; "Built on UPI Reserve Pay, the system allows users to give a one-time, consent-based authorization by setting spending limits for a merchant."; "no need for repeated PIN prompts"; users retain "full visibility, control, and the ability to revoke consent instantly"; status "Currently in a pilot phase with a select group of users" with a "Sign up for early access" CTA. Zomato, Swiggy and Zepto are the only merchants named. NPCI's participation is attested by NPCI itself, not just Razorpay — Business Today carries an on-record quote from NPCI Executive Director Sohini Rajola: "UPI Reserve Pay allows users to give consent once and permit intelligent systems to transact on their behalf in a controlled, transparent way"; Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur: "AI shouldn't stop at recommendations—it should finish the job." The Paypers independently reports the same mechanism: "a single spending limit per merchant, enabling multiple subsequent transactions without requiring a PIN entry for each purchase." UPI Reserve Pay is independently real — NPCI's rebranding of UPI Single Block Multiple Debits, circular-governed, one block per merchant per customer, MAX BLOCK Rs 10,000 (a hard ceiling Razorpay's post does not surface, and one that materially bounds what any agent can spend). Zero occurrences of "Unified Agent Protocol" or "UAP" on the announcement, which is chronologically coherent since UAP surfaced publicly only in July 2026. CAVEATS: these three are "initial partners", not a closed set; the pilot is limited-user with no announced broader-rollout timeline, so a project cannot actually transact against it; no Anthropic-side announcement was located, so avoid writing "Anthropic announced"; and Reserve Pay vs UAP is not an architectural either/or — UAP is an agent registration/verification layer that could sit above Reserve Pay-style consent.

findings.claim: Claim 5, other pilots (Vodafone in-app checkout, Gnani.ai and SuperU voice payments, Replit international payments) — UNVERIFIED in this pass. A claim naming the in-app agentic commerce partners as Zomato, Swiggy, PVR Inox, Vodafone Idea, Bluestone and Honasa failed adversarial verification 0-3, and no primary source for the Gnani.ai or Replit pilots was established.
findings.vote: 0-3 on the in-app partner list; Gnani.ai/Replit never independently sourced
findings.evidence: The only verified adjacent fact is that SuperU appears as a named partner powering one Abandoned Cart Conversion variant in Agent Studio — which is an agent partnership, not a voice-AI payments pilot, and must not be conflated with one. A separate risk flagged by verifiers: the in-app agentic commerce line (reported with partners including PVR Inox) is a DIFFERENT product from the agentic-UPI-on-Claude pilot, and merging the two merchant lists would wrongly add PVR Inox to the Claude pilot. Treat the Vodafone, Gnani.ai and Replit elements of Claim 5 as unconfirmed and do not cite them in a submission without a fresh primary check.

findings.claim: Claim 6 (Vulcan) — CONFIRMED on naming and use cases, with corrections on the data figure and a material omission. Razorpay Vulcan was announced 18 August 2026 as "India's first AI Payments Foundation Model", targeting routing, fraud and checkout conversion — but it was built with NVIDIA and AWS (which Claim 6 omits), and the ~4 billion figure is Razorpay's annual C2M transaction volume feeding a corpus of ~3 trillion data points, not a stated training-set size.
findings.vote: 3-0 on naming; two sub-claims on the 4bn framing and the exact use-case list were voted down 0-3
findings.evidence: Primary blog verbatim: "Today, we are thrilled to announce the Razorpay Vulcan, India's first AI Payments Foundation Model, purpose-built specifically to make every digital payment more reliable, safer, and predictable." A dedicated product page exists at razorpay.com/foundation-model/ titled "Razorpay Vulcan: India's First AI Payments Foundation Model", so the name is a durable product identity. Reported specifics: trained on nearly three trillion data points from four billion payments, ~3,000 signals per transaction; capabilities described as "Hyper-Precision Routing", network-level fraud protection, and dynamic checkout method recommendation / offer targeting — matching Claim 6's routing / fraud / checkout triad. Reported pilot result: 8-10% lift in payment success rates across 1.5M+ transactions and 50,000+ merchants, with named merchants Blinkit, redBus and Bachatt. Built with NVIDIA and AWS. TIMING: announced only six days before today's date, i.e. DURING the buildathon window — this is the freshest possible signal of Razorpay's AI priorities and a submission that engages with routing/fraud/checkout-conversion framing is aligned with what Razorpay just shipped. SKEPTICAL COUNTERPOINT worth knowing: Medianama's coverage ("But what does it train on?") challenges the training-data provenance and privacy story rather than the launch itself — a builder should expect that question in a panel interview.

findings.claim: Claim 7 (MCP server) — CONFIRMED WITH A NUMERIC CORRECTION. The repo README's tools table enumerates EXACTLY 45 uniquely named tools (as of main, 2026-08-24), while razorpay.com/docs/mcp-server/ headlines "35+ tools" — so "roughly 45" is defensible from the repo but is never a Razorpay-published figure. Test-mode keys are officially supported and the server auto-detects environment from the key prefix.
findings.vote: 3-0 on the count/ambiguity; 2-1 on the test-key mechanism
findings.evidence: Docs verbatim: "The Razorpay MCP Server provides comprehensive access to Razorpay APIs through 35+ tools covering:" followed by eight categories only, no tool names, no total. Raw README (curl, 18,966 bytes) machine-counted: exactly 45 table rows, 45 unique backticked names, and the README states no aggregate total ("the following tools"), so any "45" is a reader's count. FAQ verbatim on test mode: "For test mode, use test environment API keys (starting with rzp_test_). For live mode, use production API keys (starting with rzp_live_). ... The MCP Server automatically detects the environment based on your API keys." Config via env vars RAZORPAY_KEY_ID / RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET or CLI flags --key-id rzp_test_yourkeyid --key-secret yoursecretkey. MECHANISM EXPLAINING THE 35-vs-45 GAP (not a contradiction — 45 satisfies "35+"): the README has a "Remote Server Support" column; 41 of 45 rows carry a check, and FOUR are NOT available on the hosted/remote server — create_refund, close_qr_code, create_instant_settlement, create_registration_link. Local deployment is documented for those who "need access to all tools (including those restricted in the remote server)". One verifier reported a higher count (~57) from a different enumeration method; the exact 45-row table count from raw README is the better-evidenced figure. Contradiction search found no reports of rzp_test_ keys failing; the only adjacent issues (razorpay-node #10, #65, #386) are mismatched key/secret pairs, which confirm rather than contradict prefix-based mode selection. ACTIONABLE: cite "45 tools as of Aug 2026 (repo main); Razorpay docs say 35+", and cite the FAQ URL not the landing page for the test-key behaviour. QUALIFY "end-to-end demo" to payments, orders, refunds, payment links and QR flows — settlement-recon and dispute tooling return thin or empty test-mode data, which directly constrains Track 3 (Revenue Recovery) and Track 2 (Risk) scoping in a ~12-day window.

findings.claim: The MCP server's concrete action surface for an agent, verified name-by-name: payments (incl. initiate_payment, resend_otp, submit_otp), orders, refunds, payment links, QR codes, settlements (incl. fetch_settlement_recon_details, create_instant_settlement), payouts, saved-method tokens, and integration helpers detect_stack / integrate_razorpay_checkout.
findings.evidence: Full verified list from the README table: Payments — capture_payment, fetch_payment, fetch_payment_card_details, fetch_all_payments, update_payment, initiate_payment ("Initiate a payment using saved payment method with order and customer details"), resend_otp, submit_otp. Payment Links — create_payment_link, create_payment_link_upi, fetch_all_payment_links, fetch_payment_link, send_payment_link, update_payment_link. Orders — create_order, fetch_order, fetch_all_orders, update_order, fetch_order_payments. Refunds — create_refund, fetch_refund, fetch_all_refunds, update_refund, fetch_multiple_refunds_for_payment, fetch_specific_refund_for_payment. QR Codes — create_qr_code, fetch_qr_code, fetch_all_qr_codes, fetch_qr_codes_by_customer_id, fetch_qr_codes_by_payment_id, fetch_payments_for_qr_code, close_qr_code. Settlements — fetch_all_settlements, fetch_settlement_with_id, fetch_settlement_recon_details ("Fetch settlement reconciliation report"), create_instant_settlement, fetch_all_instant_settlements, fetch_instant_settlement_with_id. Payouts — fetch_all_payouts, fetch_payout_by_id. Tokens — fetch_tokens ("Get all saved payment methods by customer ID or contact number"), revoke_token. Plus create_registration_link, detect_stack, integrate_razorpay_checkout (Docker MCP Catalog note: "detect_stack ... always call this tool FIRST before calling integrate_razorpay_checkout"). SOURCING CORRECTION: razorpay.com/docs/mcp-server/ does NOT contain these names (client-side rendered); the correct primary citation is the GitHub README. NOTE: "tokens" here are saved-payment-method tokens (card/UPI recurring), not auth tokens. ACTIONABLE FOR TRACK SELECTION: fetch_settlement_recon_details is the single most Track-04-relevant tool (settlement reconciliation), and the absence of any dispute/chargeback tool in the MCP surface is a real gap for Track 02/03 builds that plan to lean on MCP.

findings.claim: Gap B (error taxonomy) — SUBSTANTIVELY FILLED and the strongest actionable finding in this report. Razorpay publishes a structured, method-specific, machine-readable failure taxonomy: per-method code lists for cards and UPI, an error-parameters page documenting the object fields (code, description, field, source, step, reason, metadata) with ENUMERATED per-method `source` values, and a downloadable spreadsheet of all reason values with next-best-action.
findings.vote: 2-1 on the structured-taxonomy claim, 3-0 on the method-specific pages, 2-1 on the UPI code list
findings.evidence: Hub page verbatim: "Below are the top error codes associated with various payment methods, along with their reasons, descriptions and steps for resolution." UPI page ("UPI Error Codes") documents TEN distinct snake_case codes, each with Description and Next Steps: bank_technical_error, credit_failed, gateway_technical_error, insufficient_funds, invalid_vpa ("The payment was unsuccessful due to the customer not being a valid user on the UPI App."), payment_cancelled, payment_collect_request_expired, payment_declined, payment_timed_out, vpa_resolution_failed. (Note: an earlier estimate of ~12 was inflated by non-code sub-headings such as "Partner Bank Downtime" appearing three times — 16 headings, 10 codes.) Cards page lists ~15 including payment_timed_out, gateway_technical_error ("There was a downtime on our partner bank due to which the payment has failed."), card_declined, insufficient_funds, card_not_enrolled, authentication_failed, incorrect_cvv, card_expired, transaction_limit_exceeded. The error-parameters page is the highest-value artifact for a root-cause agent: it enumerates `source` values per method — Cards: customer, business, internal, gateway, issuer_bank; UPI: customer, business, internal, customer_psp, gateway, network, issuer_bank, beneficiary_bank; Netbanking: customer, business, internal, issuer_bank; Wallet: customer, business, internal, issuer; Cardless EMI: customer, business, internal, network, issuer; Emandate: customer, bank, business, internal, gateway, issuer_bank. Verbatim: "To understand the errors and their `reasons`, it is recommended to know the `source` (stakeholders) and the `steps` involved in the payment flows." A literal machine-readable artifact exists — the rainy-day error-reasons page states "All the possible values for the `reason` parameter in the error response along with their explanation and the next best action are shown below" and Razorpay hosts the full enumeration as payments_error_reasons.xlsx. Docs pages also expose "View as Markdown" / "Copy for AI" affordances. ACTIONABLE DESIGN: a payment-degradation root-cause agent should key off the (code, reason, source, step) tuple — `source` already encodes blame attribution (issuer_bank vs customer_psp vs gateway vs customer), which is precisely the axis such an agent needs, and the .xlsx supplies the closed label set offline for eval fixtures. HARD CEILING TO ACKNOWLEDGE IN THE WRITE-UP: these are Razorpay's own NORMALISED merchant-facing reasons, not NPCI raw response codes (U30, U69, Z9, ZM, XD). Razorpay publishes NO crosswalk from snake_case reasons to NPCI codes, and several distinct bank failures collapse into a generic "Partner Bank Downtime" — so root-cause granularity is bounded at ~10 coarse UPI reasons. Sourcing NPCI's raw code space still requires NPCI. A separate stronger claim — that EVERY Razorpay error response carries a `source` field — was voted down 1-2, so state source-field availability as documented-per-method, not universal.

findings.claim: Claim 8 (NPCI Unified Agent Protocol not launched, pending RBI approval) — SUPPORTED but only indirectly, via reporting encountered while verifying the Claude pilot rather than through direct verification of the claim itself.
findings.vote: not directly voted; corroborated inside two 3-0 claims
findings.evidence: Business Standard (8-9 July 2026) reports UAP as developed/proposed and awaiting RBI approval, describing it as an agent registration and verification layer built on UPI Circle delegated payments rather than a new rail. Chronological support: UAP surfaced publicly only in July 2026, five months AFTER the Feb 2026 Razorpay/NPCI Claude pilot, and the pilot announcement contains zero occurrences of "Unified Agent Protocol" or "UAP" — which is why the pilot necessarily runs on the already-live UPI Reserve Pay instead. Verifiers explicitly noted that "UAP not launched" is CONSISTENT with, not contradictory to, the existence of the Claude pilot. CAVEAT: this rests on a single secondary source and was not adversarially verified as a standalone claim; re-check RBI/NPCI announcements before asserting current status in a submission.

findings.claim: REFUTED and important to correct: the official page does NOT scope builds to "Razorpay test-mode APIs". The frequently repeated framing of Track 01 as "build an agent that grows revenue for a merchant on Razorpay test-mode APIs" is not supported by the page, so test-mode limitations are a practical engineering constraint, not a stated rule of the competition.
findings.evidence: Three verifiers independently failed to sustain the test-mode-scoping claim against the primary page. Consequences for strategy: (a) do not write a submission that justifies scope limits by citing a non-existent official test-mode rule; (b) nothing on the page forbids using synthetic or public datasets, simulated ledgers, or non-Razorpay data sources — which materially widens what is buildable in a short window, especially for Tracks 02, 03 and 04 where test-mode settlement and dispute data are thin; (c) the actual binding constraints are the five "the bar" statements, which demand batch-level measured outcomes and audit trails — achievable on synthetic data, and arguably easier to demonstrate honestly there than on sparse test-mode records.

findings.claim: Gaps A, C, D, E, F, G and H were NOT filled by any claim that survived verification. No verified findings exist on test-mode simulation capabilities (Gap A), usable public datasets and licences (Gap C), competitor recon on GitHub/Devpost/LinkedIn/X/YouTube (Gap D), 2026 statements by Razorpay leaders on what gives a project "signal" (Gap E), Razorpay/NPCI/RBI business metrics on success rates, RTO and DSO (Gap F), agent evaluation and audit-trail practice under Indian regulation (Gap G), or past winners and interns (Gap H).
findings.evidence: Of 18 surviving claims, 17 concern the numbered claims 1-8 and one concerns Gap B. The verification pass was overwhelmingly weighted toward validating/refuting the numbered factual claims, leaving the higher-value research gaps essentially unaddressed. The only fragments that touch these gaps incidentally: Gap A is partially informed by the MCP finding that settlement-recon and dispute tooling return thin or empty test-mode data, and by the four tools unavailable on the remote MCP server; Gap F is partially informed by the Vulcan figures (8-10% payment success lift across 1.5M+ transactions and 50,000+ merchants; ~4bn C2M payments/year; NPCI Rs 10,000 Reserve Pay block cap); Gap G is partially informed by the Track 01 and Track 03 bars, which make "audit trail", "bounded and gated" money actions, "stopping rules" and "compliant escalation" explicit evaluation requirements, and by RBI approval being the gate on NPCI UAP. Gap D in particular — what competitors have already published — remains a complete blind spot and is the highest-value unresolved item given a ~12-day window.

result.caveats:
TIME SENSITIVITY IS SEVERE. Today is 2026-08-24 and the alleged deadline is ~12 days out. Agent Studio's early-access status, the Claude agentic-UPI pilot's scope, and the MCP server's tool count (repo main is actively changing) are all point-in-time facts verified today; each should be re-checked immediately before being cited in a submission or interview. Vulcan launched only six days ago, so coverage of it is still thin and largely derived from one announcement.

TWO CLAIMS ARE NEGATIVE FINDINGS ABOUT A PRIMARY SOURCE, WITH A SCOPE HOLE. The deadline and team-size findings verify only that razorpay.com/buildathon/ and the linked Google Form say nothing. Razorpay's LinkedIn, X and Instagram feeds could not be read directly in this pass. It remains entirely possible Razorpay stated 5 September or a team policy in a social post. Do not report "there is no deadline" — report "no deadline is published on the official page or form, and the 5 Sept date traces only to aggregators".

FIRST-PARTY DEPENDENCE. The Claude Agent SDK attribution, the agent roster, the Vulcan capability claims and the pilot descriptions all originate with Razorpay. Third-party trade coverage (Business Standard, The Paypers, Inc42, Entrackr, BW Disrupt, Fintech Singapore, Storyboard18) is demonstrably reprinting the same press releases rather than independently verifying. The two genuine exceptions are the on-record NPCI executive quote in Business Today, and the NPCI Reserve Pay circular, which independently establish the rail's existence and its Rs 10,000 cap. Performance numbers (8-10% success-rate lift) are vendor-reported and unaudited.

SPLIT VOTES AND CORRECTIONS TO CARRY FORWARD. Three findings rest on 2-1 votes (MCP test-key mechanism, the structured-taxonomy framing, the UPI code list). Four numeric or list details were corrected during verification and the corrected versions should be used: 45 MCP tools (not ~45-51, and not the ~57 one verifier counted by a different method); 10 UPI error codes (not ~12); 8 Agent Studio tiles / 7 distinct agents (with the newsroom release naming only 4); and ~4bn payments as annual C2M volume feeding a ~3-trillion-datapoint corpus rather than a stated training-set size. A stronger claim that every Razorpay error response carries a `source` field failed verification 1-2 — state source availability as documented per method.

CONFLATION RISKS. Three distinct Razorpay agentic product lines are easy to merge wrongly: (1) agentic UPI on Claude with NPCI (Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto); (2) in-app agentic commerce / Agentic Checkout (reported partners include PVR Inox and, unverified here, Vodafone Idea); (3) Agent Studio prebuilt agents (partners SuperU, Nugget by Zomato). SuperU appearing as an Agent Studio partner is NOT evidence of a SuperU voice-payments pilot. Similarly, UPI Reserve Pay and NPCI's UAP are not competing rails — UAP is a registration/verification layer that could sit above Reserve Pay-style consent.

COVERAGE IMBALANCE. Seven of the eight lettered research gaps produced no surviving verified findings. This report is therefore strong on claim adjudication and weak on the competitive and strategic intelligence that the original brief identified as the higher-value half. Anyone relying on this should treat Gaps A, C, D, E, F, G and H as still open, not as answered in the negative.
openQuestions: Did Razorpay ever state the 5 September 2026 deadline on its own LinkedIn, X or Instagram accounts? These feeds were never read directly, and this single unresolved question determines whether the submission window is ~12 days or open-ended/rolling. Highest-priority next check.

What can actually be simulated in Razorpay test mode (Gap A) — specifically failed payments with specific error codes, UPI mandate/AutoPay failures, chargebacks and disputes, settlement reconciliation reports, and webhook delivery? The MCP finding hints that settlement-recon and dispute data are thin in test mode, and that create_refund and create_instant_settlement are unavailable on the remote MCP server, but Razorpay's official test-mode, test-card and webhook-simulation docs were never fetched. This directly determines which of the five tracks is buildable end-to-end in the remaining window.

What have competitors already published (Gap D)? No search of GitHub, Devpost, LinkedIn, X or YouTube for "razorpay buildathon" / "razorpay ai builder internship" was performed, so the quality bar set by existing public submissions is completely unknown.

Is there a published crosswalk from Razorpay's ~10 normalised snake_case UPI reasons to NPCI's raw response codes (U30, U69, Z9, ZM, XD)? Verifiers established Razorpay publishes none. Whether NPCI publishes a usable public list determines the achievable granularity ceiling for any payment-degradation root-cause agent, and whether the coarse "Partner Bank Downtime" collapse can be worked around.

refuted.claim: The official page explicitly scopes builds to Razorpay TEST-MODE APIs — e.g. Track 01 asks builders to "Build an agent that grows revenue for a merchant on Razorpay test-mode APIs" — making test-mode capability (simulated failures, webhooks, settlements) the binding constraint on what is buildable.

At launch (12 March 2026, FTX'26, Bengaluru) Razorpay Agent Studio shipped FOUR named prebuilt agents — Abandoned Cart Conversion, Dispute Responder, Subscription Recovery, and Cashflow Forecaster — not seven. The launch release contains no mention of RTO Shield, RTO Insights, or Settlement Insights, so the '7 prebuilt agents' figure in Claim 4 is not supported by the launch announcement (those three, if real, were added later or appear only on the product page).

The launch release describes the agents as 'production-ready' and contains no statement that Agent Studio is in beta, early access, or waitlist-gated — so the 'beta/early access' portion of Claim 4 is UNVERIFIED (and mildly contradicted in tone) by this primary source.

Razorpay's in-app agentic commerce pilots named in the launch release are Zomato, Swiggy, PVR Inox, Vodafone Idea, Bluestone and Honasa (The Derma Co) — confirming the Vodafone (Idea) in-app checkout and Swiggy/Zomato elements of Claim 5, but the release does not mention Zepto, NPCI, Gnani.ai, or Replit international payments.

The scale figure underpinning Vulcan is ~4 billion customer-to-merchant payments per year, though the post states this as Razorpay's annual transaction volume rather than explicitly as the model's training-set size — a nuance worth flagging against the '~4 billion payments trained on' framing of Claim 6.

Vulcan's stated applications are exactly the three named in Claim 6 — payment routing, fraud detection, and checkout conversion/personalisation — described as Hyper-Precision Routing, network-level fraud protection, and dynamic checkout method recommendation.

Every Razorpay error response carries a `source` field that identifies which party in the payment chain originated the failure and who must act — enabling automated attribution of a failure to issuer vs. gateway vs. merchant vs. customer without external enrichment.
